1.explanation: To integrate Cherow, Prettier must: 1) implement a Cherow parser shim (new file parser-cherow.js in language-js, modeled on parser-babel.js); 2) update src/language-js/index.js to recognize the "cherow" parser key and call the new implementation; 3) register the new parser in src/main/multiparser.js so the core multiplexer will pick it; 4) add the parser name to src/languages.js and src/cli/constant.js so the CLI and parser inference know about it; 5) include Cherow in the standalone bundles (standalone.js and src/standalone.js) and in the playground worker (website/static/worker.js); 6) update tests_config/utils/check-parsers.js to allow the new parser; and 7) adjust the bin/prettier.js CLI stub to report the new parser option. Without touching all of these, Prettier cannot expose or use Cherow to speed up JS parsing.
1.bug_scenario: Prettier currently uses the Babel (Babylon) parser for JavaScript, which benchmarks show is substantially slower than Cherow. In a format-on-save workflow, parsing time dominates UX. The user’s benchmark in the screenshot confirms Cherow is about 40% faster than Babylon across large JS files. They want Prettier to support a Cherow-based JS parser (with Flow support added later) so that formatting speed improves without changing end-user API.

2.explanation:
All of these files participate in discovering, registering, and invoking JS parsers in Prettier. 

• src/language-js/parser-babel.js is where Prettier wraps the Babel/Flow parser. To use Cherow instead you either replace or add a new parser file here.  
• src/language-js/options.js and src/language-js/index.js define which parser names (e.g. “babel”, “flow”, “typescript”) are exposed to the CLI and config — they must include “cherow” or swap the default.  
• src/main/parser.js is the central dispatcher that calls a parser by name — it needs a new case to invoke Cherow’s parseScript API.  
• src/languages.js lists all supported languages and their parser aliases — it must be updated so that “javascript” can resolve the “cherow” parser.  
• tests_config/utils/check-parsers.js enforces that every declared parser actually exists. Adding “cherow” or swapping out “babel” requires updating this test utility so CI doesn’t break.
2.bug_scenario: Prettier currently uses Babel (Babylon) as its default JavaScript parser, which is relatively slow. The benchmark screenshot shows that the Cherow parser is about 40% faster than Babylon across several large JS libraries (jquery, angular, react, typescript). The user wants to swap in Cherow (or at least offer it as an option) so that format-on-save in editors becomes noticeably snappier.
